answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can vote on payments, with rewards weighted by stake and withheld until a dispute window closes. A zephyr of new accounts then adds little influence unless the attacker buys or ties up more capital; suspicious clusters can have their kernel of shared funding traced and slashed when fraud is proven. A sparrow-sized attacker can still join, but cannot cheaply multiply its voting power.
